ai_ml_dl.description: Nested circles: AI contains machine learning contains deep learning; data science overlaps.
ai_ml_dl.alt: Nested circles showing deep learning inside machine learning inside artificial intelligence, with data science overlapping them.

order_value_hist.description: Histogram of order value with mean and median marked (real, Lakeside orders).
order_value_hist.alt: Histogram of order values. Most orders are small, a long tail runs right, and the mean lies to the right of the median.

distribution_shapes.description: Three distribution shapes (symmetric, right-skewed, two humps) with mean and median lines (schematic from simulated data).
distribution_shapes.alt: Three histograms: a symmetric one where mean and median match, a right-skewed one where the mean is larger, and a two-peaked one.

boxplot_anatomy.description: Annotated box plot: median, quartiles, whiskers, outliers (schematic).
boxplot_anatomy.alt: A box plot labelled with median, first and third quartile, whiskers and outliers.

revenue_by_month.description: Monthly revenue line 2024-2025 with December highlighted (real).
revenue_by_month.alt: Line chart of monthly revenue across two years, peaking sharply every December.

revenue_by_branch.description: Horizontal bars of sample revenue by branch (real).
revenue_by_branch.alt: Horizontal bar chart of revenue for each of the eight branches, largest at Kampala Central.

box_by_branch.description: Box plot of order value by branch (real).
box_by_branch.alt: Box plots of order value for each branch; the boxes are similar and many high-value outliers sit above them.

returns_count_vs_rate.description: Two panels: returns COUNT by branch and returns RATE by branch; the leaders differ (real).
returns_count_vs_rate.alt: Two bar charts. By count, Kampala Central has the most returns. By rate, Fort Portal is highest.

bad_vs_good_axis.description: The same four bars on a truncated axis and on a zero-based axis (schematic, made-up values).
bad_vs_good_axis.alt: Two bar charts of the same data. With a cut axis the difference looks huge; from zero it is small.

category_revenue.description: Bars of revenue by product category (real).
category_revenue.alt: Bar chart of sample revenue by product category; staples and phones and electronics lead.

payment_split.description: Bars: share of orders by payment method (real).
payment_split.alt: Bar chart of the share of orders paid by cash, mobile money and card.

sampling_means.description: 200 sample means of 30 orders each, with the true mean marked (real, seeded simulation).
sampling_means.alt: Histogram of 200 sample means, each from 30 random orders, centred near the true mean and spread out around it.

sampling_n_compare.description: Sample means for n = 5, 30 and 200 on one axis: bigger samples, narrower spread (real, seeded).
sampling_n_compare.alt: Three histograms of sample means for sample sizes 5, 30 and 200. The spread narrows as the sample grows.

footfall_orders_scatter.description: Scatter of weekly footfall vs orders per branch-week with fitted line (real).
footfall_orders_scatter.alt: Scatter plot of weekly orders against footfall for each branch-week with an upward fitted line.

rain_orders_scatter.description: Scatter of weekly rainfall vs orders (real); a weaker, downward link.
rain_orders_scatter.alt: Scatter plot of weekly orders against rainfall with a gently downward fitted line and a lot of scatter.

confounding.description: Causal diagram: a hidden third factor (season) drives both ice-cream style sales and another measure (schematic).
confounding.alt: Diagram with a hidden factor, hot weather, pointing to both ice cream sales and drownings, which look linked but are not causal.

ab_test_ci.description: Mean next-month spend, offer vs control, with 95 percent intervals (real).
ab_test_ci.alt: Two bars with error bars of next-month spend for offer and control groups; the intervals nearly touch.

difference_ci.description: The offer lift as a difference with its 95 percent interval and a zero line (real).
difference_ci.alt: A point with an interval showing the spend difference between offer and control, entirely to the right of zero.

pvalue_curve.description: Bell curve with the extreme tails shaded: what a p-value measures (schematic, standard normal).
pvalue_curve.alt: A bell curve with both tails shaded to show the chance of a result at least this extreme if nothing is going on.

regression_fit.description: Footfall vs orders with the least-squares line and three residuals drawn (real).
regression_fit.alt: Scatter with a fitted line and vertical segments from three points to the line showing residuals.

residual_plot.description: Residuals vs fitted values for the weekly orders model (real): a healthy random cloud.
residual_plot.alt: Scatter of residuals against fitted values forming an even cloud around zero.

coef_forest.description: Coefficients of the weekly orders model with 95 percent intervals (real, statsmodels will match).
coef_forest.alt: Dot-and-interval plot of three regression coefficients: footfall up, promotion up, rain down.

class_imbalance.description: Bars: loans repaid vs defaulted, showing the 87 to 13 imbalance (real).
class_imbalance.alt: Two bars showing most loans are repaid and about one in eight defaults.

default_by_occupation.alt: Bar chart of the share of loans that default for each occupation.

default_by_burden.description: Default rate by repayment-burden band (instalment as a share of income) (real).
default_by_burden.alt: Bar chart showing default rate rising with repayment burden.

sigmoid_curve.description: The logistic S-curve turning any score into a probability, with a 0.5 threshold (schematic).
sigmoid_curve.alt: S-shaped curve from 0 to 1 with a dashed line at 0.5 showing where the model switches from no to yes.

threshold_tradeoff.description: Precision and recall as the decision threshold moves, for the loan model (real, numpy logistic regression).
threshold_tradeoff.alt: Two curves: recall falls and precision rises as the threshold increases.

roc_honest_vs_leaky.description: ROC curves: honest features (AUC about 0.76) vs the leaked collection_calls column (AUC about 0.99) (real, numpy logistic regression).
roc_honest_vs_leaky.alt: Two ROC curves. The leaky model hugs the top-left corner, far above the honest model.

overfit_curve.description: Train and test error as a model gets more flexible; test error eventually shoots up (real weekly orders, polynomial degree 1 to 12).
overfit_curve.alt: Two curves: training error stays low and flat as flexibility grows, while test error stays close at first and then jumps up and runs off the chart.

feature_weights.description: Standardised weights of the honest loan model, biggest first (real, numpy logistic regression).
feature_weights.alt: Horizontal bars of the strongest weights in the loan model: repayment burden and late payments push risk up, savings and group loans push it down.

decision_tree_schematic.description: A small decision tree drawn as rules about a borrower (schematic; thresholds illustrative).
decision_tree_schematic.alt: A three-level decision tree of yes and no questions about repayment burden, late payments and savings that ends in low, medium and high risk.

train_test_split.description: One dataset split into training and test parts (schematic bar).
train_test_split.alt: A long bar divided into a larger training part and a smaller test part held back.

cv_folds.description: Five-fold cross-validation: each fold takes a turn as the test part (schematic).
cv_folds.alt: Five bars, each with a different fifth highlighted as the test fold.

kmeans_segments.description: Customers on recency and spend, coloured by k-means segment (real, numpy k-means, k = 4).
kmeans_segments.alt: Scatter of customers by days since last order and total spend, coloured in four segments.

elbow_plot.description: Within-cluster spread against k for customer segments, to choose k (real, numpy k-means).
elbow_plot.alt: Line chart of within-cluster error falling as the number of clusters grows, with a bend near four.

pca_view.description: Customer features flattened to two axes with PCA, coloured by segment (real, numpy SVD).
pca_view.alt: Scatter of customers on two principal components, coloured by segment, showing separated groups.

segment_profile.description: Average recency, frequency and spend per segment, scaled 0 to 1 (real, numpy k-means).
segment_profile.alt: Grouped bars comparing recency, frequency and spend across four customer segments.

clinic_season.description: Malaria cases by calendar month across all districts (real).
clinic_season.alt: Bar chart of malaria cases for each month with peaks after the two rainy seasons.

rain_lag_scatter.description: Malaria cases against rainfall in the same month and the month before (real); the lag fits better.
rain_lag_scatter.alt: Two scatter plots. Same-month rainfall shows no pattern; last month rainfall shows an upward pattern.

ts_decomposition.description: Trend, seasonal pattern and leftover noise of total monthly malaria cases (real).
ts_decomposition.alt: Three stacked panels showing a rising trend, a repeating yearly pattern and small leftover noise.

clinic_forecast.description: Seasonal-naive forecast against actual for the last 12 months of one district, with MAE (real).
clinic_forecast.alt: Line chart with actual cases and a seasonal-naive forecast that repeats last year, closely following the pattern.

time_split.description: Time-ordered train and test split for a time series (schematic).
time_split.alt: A timeline where the early months are training data and the later months are the test data.

activation_functions.description: Sigmoid, tanh and ReLU curves side by side (schematic).
activation_functions.alt: Three small plots of the sigmoid, tanh and ReLU activation functions.

nn_diagram.description: A small feed-forward network: inputs, two hidden layers, one output (schematic).
nn_diagram.alt: Diagram of a neural network with three input nodes, two hidden layers of four nodes and one output node, all connected.

text_map.description: Customer feedback messages placed in 2D from their word counts (real TF-IDF + SVD), coloured by sentiment.
text_map.alt: Scatter of customer messages positioned by word usage, with positive, negative and neutral messages forming loose groups.

dataframe_anatomy.description: Head of the orders table with its parts named: columns, rows, index, one cell (real values).
dataframe_anatomy.alt: A small table of the first orders with arrows naming the column names, row index and a single cell.

split_apply_combine.description: GROUP BY as split, apply, combine, drawn with real branch totals (schematic of real numbers).
split_apply_combine.alt: Diagram: a table is split into groups by branch, each group is summed, and the sums combine into a small result table.

join_types.description: Four join types as overlapping circles with the rows each keeps (schematic).
join_types.alt: Four small Venn diagrams for inner, left, right and outer joins with the kept area shaded.

join_doubling.description: Why a join can double revenue: one order row matched to two rows (schematic with real-looking IDs).
join_doubling.alt: Two small tables joined on order_id where a duplicate key in the second table produces two result rows for one order.

sql_order.description: The order SQL is written in versus the order it runs (schematic).
sql_order.alt: Two lists side by side: the written order of SQL clauses and the order the database actually runs them.

ml_workflow.description: The machine learning workflow as a loop (schematic).
ml_workflow.alt: A loop of steps: question, data, features, split, train, evaluate, then improve or deliver.

sklearn_pipeline.description: A scikit-learn Pipeline as connected blocks (schematic).
sklearn_pipeline.alt: Blocks in a row: impute missing values, scale numbers, encode categories, then fit a model, all packed into one pipeline.

drift_chart.description: Average borrower income over time with a shift that makes an old model go stale (schematic, simulated).
drift_chart.alt: Line chart of a monthly average that is steady and then drops, with a label showing the point where the model should be re-checked.

rag_pipeline.description: Retrieval before answering: question, search the documents, pass the best passages to the model (schematic).
rag_pipeline.alt: Pipeline: a question becomes a vector, the closest document passages are found, and a language model answers using only those passages.

embedding_idea.description: Meaning as position: similar phrases sit close together on a 2D map (schematic with example phrases).
embedding_idea.alt: A two-dimensional map where phrases about queues sit near each other, away from phrases about prices and about payment.

token_example.description: A sentence cut into tokens with made-up token numbers (schematic, labelled illustrative).
token_example.alt: A sentence split into word and word-piece boxes, each with an identification number underneath.

learning_path.description: A six-month learning path after the course, from practice to portfolio (schematic).
learning_path.alt: Three-step path with months one to two, three to four and five to six listing practice, depth and portfolio goals.

missing_by_column.description: Count of missing values per column in the loans file (real).
missing_by_column.alt: Bar chart of missing values per column; only monthly income has missing entries.

chart_choice.description: Which chart for which question (schematic of four mini charts).
chart_choice.alt: Four mini charts with labels: histogram for one number, bar for a comparison, line for change over time, scatter for two numbers.

loop_vs_fill.alt: Left: a spreadsheet column with a formula dragged down. Right: a Python for loop doing the same for each item.
